titulo: I would like you to come
intro: Use the imperfect subjunctive after a wish or request in the conditional.
p.quisiera que: I would like someone to; I wish someone would
b1.texto: With verbs of desire or request, use **que + subjunctive** when the subordinate clause has a different subject: **Quiero que vengas**; **Me gustaría que vinieras**. When both clauses have the same subject, use the infinitive: **Me gustaría viajar**. A change of subject by itself does not choose the subjunctive; the meaning and the expression that introduces the clause matter. Compare **Creo que viene** with **No creo que venga**. Form the imperfect subjunctive from the third-person plural of the preterite: **hablaron → hablara**, **comieron → comiera**, **vivieron → viviera**. The **-ra** forms are common; **-se** forms also exist (**viniese**). The past-looking form does not necessarily describe a past event: after **gustaría**, it can express a present or future wish.
b3.f0: I would like you to come for lunch on Sunday.
b3.f1: I'd love to, but I work in the morning.
b3.f2: I would like you to meet my sister. She arrives on Saturday.
b3.f3: If I could change my shift, I would go without a problem.
b4.f0: Marcos works in a restaurant and almost always gets his schedule only a few days in advance.
b4.f1: He would like his manager to post them a week earlier.
b4.f2: His colleague Inés would prefer the team to have two days off in a row once a month.
b4.f3: They are not asking for longer holidays: they want to plan ahead.
b4.f4: If they spoke to their manager, they might find a solution.
b4.f5: On Friday they are going to ask for a short meeting.
b6.pregunta: Complete: I would like you to come.
b6.o0.refuerzo: A different subject after me gustaría que takes the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Use an infinitive when both clauses have the same subject.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The conditional does not follow que here.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I would like to travel.
b7.o0.refuerzo: The same person has the wish and would travel.
b7.o1.refuerzo: This would need a different subject, such as que ella viajara.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive follows me gustaría when the subject is the same.
b8.pregunta: Which form completes the request: quisiera que ustedes ___ más temprano?
b8.o0.refuerzo: The imperfect subjunctive agrees with ustedes.
b8.o1.refuerzo: The conditional is not used after que in this request.
b8.o2.refuerzo: This is present subjunctive; the main verb is quisiera.
b9.pregunta: Why do Marcos and Inés want a change?
b9.o0.refuerzo: They want more notice of their schedules.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The text says they are not asking for longer holidays.
b9.o2.refuerzo: They plan to request a meeting.
b10.traduccion: I would prefer you to let me know in advance.
